---
title: "ADNI"
description: "Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative: longitudinal imaging, biomarker, genetic, and cognitive data. Controlled access."
---

The Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) follows older adults
across North America who are cognitively normal, have mild cognitive
impairment, or have Alzheimer's dementia. Participants return for repeated
visits, so most measures are available over time.

- **Website:** [adni.loni.usc.edu](https://adni.loni.usc.edu/)
- **Data:** the [LONI Image and Data Archive (IDA)](https://ida.loni.usc.edu/login.jsp)
- **Access:** controlled. Tomás adds lab members.

## What's in it

ADNI has run in five phases: ADNI1, ADNI-GO, ADNI2, ADNI3, and ADNI4. The data
include:

- Clinical assessments, cognitive tests, and questionnaires
- MRI and PET (amyloid, tau, FDG) images, plus processed numerical datasets
- Biofluid biomarkers from CSF and blood
- Genetics and other omics
- Neuropathology, for participants who came to autopsy

The most complete genomic and other omics data are distributed through
NIAGADS and NACC rather than the IDA; see the
[ADNI Data page](https://adni.loni.usc.edu/data-samples/adni-data/).

The [ADNI FAQ](https://adni.loni.usc.edu/help-faqs/faqs/) describes
ADNIMERGE as key ADNI tables merged into one table, available on the Study
Data page. It lists ADNI1, GO, 2, and 3, so check whether it includes ADNI4
before you rely on it for ADNI4 data.

### ADNI4

ADNI4, the current phase, began enrolling in 2023. It aims to make ADNI more
representative of the North American population, and it adds:

- Assessments of social determinants of health
- Both amyloid and tau PET for every participant
- Expanded plasma biomarker data, new genetic data, and new MRI sequences
- Digital neuropathology: digitized slides of specific brain regions
- Remote cohorts: people screened from home with online questionnaires and
  cognitive tests (Remote Digital Cohort) or blood biomarkers (Remote Blood
  Cohort). Their data are also shared through the IDA.

See the [ADNI4 page](https://adni.loni.usc.edu/about/adni4/) for details.

## Publishing with ADNI data

According to the [ADNI FAQ](https://adni.loni.usc.edu/help-faqs/faqs/), every
manuscript that uses ADNI data must:

- Be sent to the ADNI Data Sharing and Publications Committee (DPC) before you
  submit it to a journal. The review checks that ADNI is cited correctly and
  can take up to two weeks, so plan for it.
- Include ADNI in the author line.
- Use ADNI's required wording in the methods and acknowledgments.

Take the wording from ADNI's
[manuscript citation guidelines](https://adni.loni.usc.edu/wp-content/themes/adni_2023/documents/ADNI_Manuscript_Citations.pdf)
and see the
[Data Sharing and Publication Policy](https://adni.loni.usc.edu/wp-content/themes/adni_2023/documents/ADNI_DSP_Policy.pdf)
for the full rules. Don't copy it from an older paper, which may use outdated
wording.
